name: Drop the unused npm React dependencies that carry the node-fetch advisory
request: Drop the unused npm React dependencies that carry the node-fetch advisory
checks: npm run check passed: typecheck, build, 725 tests 0 fail, doc links in 18 files, validate-build 34 files and 5 React entry points; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities
result: Removed react and react-dom from package.json dependencies: nothing imports them (zero 'from "react"' matches in src/ or extension/), the runtime is the hand-placed extension/vendor/*.production.min.js that validate-build.mjs asserts every page loads, and scripts/package.mjs excludes node_modules from the installer. Their only effect was pulling fbjs -> isomorphic-fetch -> node-fetch <2.6.7, five high-severity advisories that no code path could reach. npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities with no 'audit fix --force', which was rejected because it installs react 16.14.0 and would leave package.json declaring a version the extension does not run. The two version numbers are preserved in a new 'vendoredRuntime' field that npm ignores. ALSO FIXED, found because it broke the verification: scripts/build.mjs passed an absolute -p path to tsc with shell:true on Windows, so a checkout under a path containing spaces ('linkdin version v2') was re-split by the shell into a project plus two stray source files - error TS5042 - after lines 11-12 had already deleted dist/ and .build/, leaving no loadable extension. The project path is now passed relative to cwd, which is already root. dist/ is rebuilt and byte-identical in what it ships: vendor/ is untouched.
